## Request

Expose purrdf's error types as structured data, so a consumer can record every variant and field
of an error, typed, without rendering it through `Display` or `Debug`.

## Why

Katamari logs structurally (its ADR-0051): every field of an error reaches the log typed -- counts
as counts, codes as codes -- and nothing is flattened to a string. Today it can do that for a
purrdf error only by mirroring the enum variant by variant on its side, as it now does for
`SegmentedError` and `StorageError`. That falls short in three ways:

1. **`#[non_exhaustive]` enums cannot be mirrored completely.** A variant purrdf adds later falls
   into the consumer's wildcard arm and is logged as "unlisted", losing its fields, until the
   consumer notices and extends its mirror. This affects `SegmentedError`, `TextError`,
   `XsdError`, `CanonError`, `EvalError`, `PackError` and `FallibleSparqlError`.
2. **Some variants carry text where the cause has structure.** For example `TextError::Config`,
   `TextError::Data`, `TextError::Overflow`, `TextError::Domain`, `EvalError::Parse`,
   `EvalError::Internal`, `EvalError::Remote`, `EvalError::ServiceUnconfigured`,
   `CanonError::Read` and `PackError::ViewNotReady { cause }` hold a `String`. A consumer
   cannot recover from that string what the producer knew when it wrote it.
3. **Nested errors multiply the mirroring.** Mirroring `TextError` means mirroring
   `CapacityFailure`, `NativeDiagnostic`, `SubstringRefusal`, `PhoneticRefusal` and the HTML
   diagnostics; `PackError` brings `PackDictError`, `PackTriplesError` and `PackSideError`;
   `EvalError` brings `RetainedServiceFailure`, `ServiceDenial` and the XPath regex error. Every
   consumer that wants structured errors repeats this, and every purrdf change silently breaks
   it.

## What would solve it

- **A structured visitor every error type implements**, for example a trait with
  `fn visit(&self, visitor: &mut dyn ErrorVisitor)`. The error reports its variant name (stable
  across releases, like a diagnostic code) and then each field by name and kind: unsigned,
  signed, boolean, static code or string, IRI or term, byte count, a nested error (visited the
  same way), or a list of these. A consumer encodes it without knowing the enum, so a new
  variant arrives with its fields intact, and `#[non_exhaustive]` stays as it is.
- **Typed causes in place of `String` payloads** wherever the producer has the structure: a
  diagnostic (`RdfDiagnostic`, which is already structured), or a small enum of the reasons
  that site can produce. Where the text genuinely is the data (a remote server's message, say),
  keep it, and mark it as such in the visitor.
- **Accessors for private fields**, where a type keeps fields private (as `CapacityError` does
  for its counts, which already has `attempted()` and `limit()`). The visitor covers this if
  each type reports its own fields.

## Scope in Katamari today

Katamari logs `SegmentedError`, `StorageError`, `CapacityError`, `NativeBuildError`,
`RdfDiagnostic`, `FallibleSparqlError`, `TextError`, `XsdError`, `CanonError`, `EvalError` and
the JSON error. Until a visitor exists, Katamari mirrors each of them on its side, with an
"unlisted" arm for variants added later.

# Preserve typed errors through a single borrowed visitor

Expose a consumer-facing visitor with stable variant identity, named typed
fields and nested/list values, without rendering an error or cloning its cause.
Complete all first-party shipping errors, the named Katamari types and known
string-flattening producers. Keep non_exhaustive enums, human presentation,
original refusal priority, physical grants and portable semantics intact.

Use purrdf-hash's zero-dependency root for the protocol and shared implementation
macro. No new external runtime dependency or semantic feature is needed. The
events protocol may depend on that root, as explicitly allowed by layers.toml,
while staying independent of the IR and GTS. Reuse lex diagnostic/constructor
homes. The inspection protocol borrows semantic data; it does not serialize
allocator addresses or make new copies of retained payloads. Root-wide scalar
types must preserve u128/i128, not narrow counters to u64 or host JSON numbers.

The shared macro must generate exhaustive own-crate patterns without wildcard
or rest patterns. A new variant or payload field then requires producer-side
inspection support to compile, while an existing consumer remains generic.
Nested causes are handed out as borrowed structured values; a consumer may use
a heap work list instead of recursive callbacks. Native source identity, codes,
counts, terms, bytes and external messages remain distinct field kinds.

No subagents are used. Owner assessments are not independent approval. Actual
hosted source review and the final equivalent full gate remain required before
merge; no simulated reviewer report or extra approval ceremony is introduced.

## Completeness contract

| Requirement | Task | Actual acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| Stable variants and all named typed fields | 1–6 | Consumer records native error values through one visitor with no enum match; exact variant/field/type/value assertions |
| Non_exhaustive evolution | 1, 7 | Same generic recorder accepts a further producer variant and fields; exhaustive producer patterns prevent omitted variants/fields |
| Full-width signed/unsigned, bool, code/text, IRI/term, bytes and lists | 1–3, 7 | Values above u64 and binary64 exact-integer range, negative values, real terms and nested heterogeneous payloads survive without formatting |
| Eleven explicitly named consumer error families | 2–5, 7 | Actual SegmentedError, StorageError, CapacityError, NativeBuildError, RdfDiagnostic, FallibleSparqlError, TextError, XsdError, CanonError, EvalError and JSON error captures |
| All other first-party shipping errors | 6 | Reviewed source inventory includes explicit and macro-generated errors, target-gated families and nested payloads; every entry has a compiled visitor and applicable execution/control |
| Known structure currently flattened to String | 3–6 | Actual invalid configuration/data, overflow/domain, parse/internal/SERVICE, canonical read and pack readiness failures expose their original codes/fields/causes |
| Genuine text remains message data | 4–7 | Remote/caller message preserves bytes and its message field kind, without pretending text is a parsed native cause |
| Private semantic fields | 2–6 | Producer-owned visitors read original private counters/payloads; consumer does not mirror private layout |
| Original grants, clone/drop, first faults and row shape | 2–7 | Existing admission/lifetime/refusal controls, zero-allocation inspection and affected layout/fixed-work controls; no timing acceptance |
| Portable and host parity | 7–8 | Native and standard scalar/SIMD WASM inspection executions, strict affected compilation and existing host error mapping controls |
| Real delivery | 8–9 | Complete hosted gate/review, ghprsq integration, verified closure/archive/mirror and delivery cleanup |

## Task 1: Borrowed inspection protocol and exhaustive shared macro

Implement the protocol once in the root, preserving exact scalar widths and
borrowed lifetimes for nested values/lists. Supply no default Display/Debug or
unlisted fallback. Wire actual root HexError and events EventError as the first
production consumers; update the events root edge and explanatory metadata.
Run focused root/event controls, zero-allocation inspection and native/portable
compilation. Review the actual interface and exhaustive field handling locally,
commit with normal hooks and publish the coherent slice to this issue branch.
No foundation-only PR or closure is permitted.

## Task 2: Foundation diagnostics and complete native scalar causes

Wire allocation, lexical/JSON/XML/HTML/CBOR/YAML, IRI, XSD, CDT and other
foundation error families through the same protocol. Preserve exact private
capacity counts, diagnostic codes/ranges/typed arguments, nested causes and
real RDF term payloads through their existing homes. Compile coherent package
slices before widening the migration. Record exact inventory coverage and
meaningful captures; commit/push after focused checks.

## Task 3: Native storage, canonicalization and retained failures

Cover native builds, segmented/paged storage, every pack sub-error and canonical
errors. Replace CanonError::Read and pack readiness strings wherever their
producer has a typed source. Keep real faults and their original owners across
fallible query boundaries; generic caller causes participate through the same
trait rather than a blanket formatter. Exercise actual corrupt-source and
capacity/refund paths, private fields and retained snapshots. Rebind unchanged
capacity proof contracts only when their actual source closure changes.

## Task 4: Evaluator and SERVICE producers

Expose all evaluator/fallible/governor/service error payloads, including retained
diagnostics, policy denials and XPath causes. Replace known parse/internal/
remote/unconfigured formatting with typed causes at production creation and
transport sites. Preserve external message data and current SILENT/operational-
failure precedence. Check actual query parse/runtime/SERVICE failures and their
complete nested captures, plus original query completion and host mappings.
Measure affected layouts before broad qualification; keep default rows stable.

## Task 5: Text configuration, data, numeric and search refusals

Replace known Config/Data/Overflow/Domain strings with typed reasons and fields,
including the actual producer values. Visit capacity/native diagnostics,
substring, phonetic and HTML diagnostics completely and preserve them when
crossing into evaluator errors. Use actual index/query failures and existing
fixed-point/refusal controls. No consumer regex-parses a human message.

## Task 6: Finish the shipping inventory and remaining producers

Inspect every remaining first-party shipping error declaration and macro-generated
error, including codecs, geometry, rules/entailment, validation, retrieval and
host-owned Rust errors. Maintain the concrete source inventory with each native
visitor, semantic fields, nested types and executed/compiled coverage. A candidate
count or a public-name search is not completeness. Adapt actual callers and
remove obsolete flattening routes; do not accumulate an uncompiled whole-tree
migration. Run affected checks and publish coherent units with normal hooks.

## Task 7: Real generic consumer and unchanged error behavior

Execute a consumer that knows only the inspection protocol on actual native
failures from every listed family. Assert variant identity, named field types,
exact wide values, nested/list contents and genuine external-message tags.
Use a caller cause whose Display/Debug panic to prove generic transport does
not format it. Exercise deep nested capture with heap traversal, normal
readiness/failure/clone/drop paths and zero-allocation inspection. Compare
existing public codes/presentation and logical results, including host paths.
Fix demonstrated regressions at their production homes.

## Task 8: Portable and final qualification

Run affected native/scalar/SIMD portable executions and strict packages, exact
allocation/layout/fixed-work controls and generated/manual metadata. Use the
normal hosted workflow as the equivalent final full gate after implementation
settles; do not duplicate a local whole-workspace suite or use elapsed-time
performance acceptance. Resolve actual material hosted review findings and
independently reported source concerns without inventing approval.

## Task 9: Publish and integrate the complete contract

Create one complete PR with the full issue closure and current evidence, post
this plan and actual results, assess the real integration base, and satisfy
required hosted checks/review. Merge only through ghprsq; verify issue closure,
selected evidence archive, mirror and immediate branch/worktree cleanup. Update
REWORK_LIST.md with real delivery accounting. No follow-up issue or opaque/string
fallback substitutes for required native structure.

Published `315806042` and `6d52a5c11` through normal hooks. The borrowed protocol
and exhaustive producer macros now inspect actual hash/event errors and six
allocation/JSON types, including private capacity counters and nested causes.

including through StorageError and the JSON error. A real lone-surrogate parse

controls reject omitted producer variants/enum fields/struct members. Affected

The helper check found duplicate panic-only test callbacks. The test recorder
now captures list metadata and end counts; updated checks pass without an
exemption. The reviewed allocation authority refresh changes no proof contract,
sink, refusal check, layout or constructor binding.

This is a partial implementation. The remaining foundation/core/evaluator/text
families, complete shipping inventory, known string-flattening producer fixes,
real host consumers, runtime portability and final hosted review/gate remain

is in progress on this same branch.

Published `cfb86417b` through normal hooks. Twelve additional lexical error and
diagnostic payload types implement the existing borrowed protocol, bringing
the implemented subset to twenty. Lexical and umbrella modules expose that
same protocol through existing dependency edges.

actual parser/scalar/YAML refusals, and diagnostic typed arguments, lists and
optional detail. Umbrella library compilation, affected strict Clippy, standard
WASM lexical compilation and the explicit-root helper check pass. No proof,
exemption, error layout, admission behavior or human presentation changed in
this unit.

The inventory explicitly distinguishes executed variants from compile-only
families. It is an implemented subset, not shipping completeness. Remaining
XML/HTML/CBOR/record and other foundation families, core/evaluator/text causes,
known string-flattening producers, full inventory, real portable/host consumers
and final hosted review/gates remain required. This branch has no PR yet.

Published `7e8dc47d5` with normal hooks. XML and HTML now expose six additional
producer/payload types through the shared visitor. All six XML namespace
production branches retain one of five typed reasons rather than allocating
a rendered native cause; their exact previous human messages are preserved.
HTML retains its standard classification and original source byte range.

All six focused native controls and all 55 XML unit tests pass. Strict affected
checks, standard WASM lexical compilation and the explicit-root helper check
pass. The initial redundant err().expect() in the new test was fixed, with no

open; this is not a whole-issue delivery or PR.

Published `6fcedbfaa` through normal hooks. CBOR's two native error types now
expose their complete variants/fields, including original offsets, configured
limits and the actual reader's I/O category. The implemented first-party subset

The root adapts standard I/O categories once: public stable categories have

Three root and seven lexical focused controls pass, including zero-allocation

Published `7f74c8ff9` through normal hooks. Twenty-two XSD error/payload types,
including the private numeric-reader error, now expose their original fields
through the shared visitor. The implemented first-party subset is 50 types;

A shared testkit consumer records ordered typed fields, unnamed entries and
list boundaries without native enum mirrors or formatting. XSD and lexical
diagnostic controls reuse it. Four XSD and seven lexical controls pass for

Owner source assessment; this is not independent approval or issue completion.

and destination allocation grant. The payload dies before its grant. Diagnostic

# Original text source-read causes
